title: Why Most Leaders Feel Lonely
paragraphs: The more you decide to be yourself, the more lonely you will become. correct. Because everyone around you wants you to be like them, or they want you to be them. So, when you discover that you are unique, special, and important, and you decide to be yourself and achieve what you have dreamed of, loneliness is the result. I say this often, and I write about it in my books, that every true vision initially finds only one believer in it. He is the person who possesses that vision. How wonderful.

This is what makes it desolate. But what attracts people to you is when you decide that you don't care about being alone, and that you will continue to pursue your vision. This is correct. So, it is the desire to make good use of your solitude that makes people come to you, so you are never alone again. Therefore, I was alone most of the time. I am alone now because the leader is always alone being at the front. There is no one there with him.

When you think about it, if everyone is around you, then you are part of the crowd. This is correct. Therefore, the leaders live lives full of solitude, but they chose this solitude. This is important. You have to choose to be alone if you want to change the world. Every great leader in history, when you study him, you find that he found his true self when he was alone. You know, Moses was in the wilderness. Jesus Christ was in the desert. Paul went into the desert.

You know, when you pursue something more important than the crowd, you end up leading that crowd. How wonderful. Someone said, "You can't conduct an orchestra unless you turn your back to the audience." Think about it for a minute. Yes, if you want to be the leader, you have to turn your back on the crowd, and then you can lead life.
